I'll check the project-issues skill since it covers merge requests on GitLab.
I have the GitLab-specific guidance from the project-issues skill, but I want to flag a limitation before answering: this session doesn't expose the underlying `get_ref`/`create_pr`/`list_projects` calls as tools I can actually invoke — the skill only returned its reference documentation both times I called it, not live GitLab data. So I can't check your actual `feature/login` branch for you right now; I can only tell you what the documented behavior is and what you should run yourself.

**What happens if you open the MR on GitLab with no real diff:**

- GitLab does **not** refuse the call the way GitHub does. It will create the merge request even if `feature/login` and `main` point at the exact same commit.
- The created MR's `detailed_merge_status` will be `"commits_status"`, and it stays unmergeable until `feature/login` actually has commits ahead of `main`.
- Critically: a "successful" `create_pr` call on GitLab is **not proof** the branches were right — GitLab will happily create an empty/no-op MR that just sits there unmergeable.
- Don't rely on the `mergeable` field either — GitLab's `mergeable` is `null` for every state except `"mergeable"`, so check `detailed_merge_status` specifically.

**What to check first, before creating anything:**

1. Call `get_ref` on `feature/login` (the head) and separately on `main` (the base) for the project.
   - If `get_ref` errors on `feature/login`, the branch isn't pushed (or the name is wrong) — fix that before doing anything else.
   - If both resolve to the **same commit sha**, `feature/login` has nothing ahead of `main` — don't open the MR yet.
   - If they resolve to **different** shas, that only proves the branches aren't identical — it does **not** prove `feature/login` is ahead. It could be behind `main` instead. `get_ref` alone can't distinguish "ahead" from "behind"; you'd need to actually look at the commit history/diff to be sure.

Since I can't run `get_ref` for you in this session, I'd suggest running it yourself (or checking `git log main..feature/login` locally if you have the repo) before opening the MR — that's the direct way to see whether there are any commits on `feature/login` that aren't already on `main`.
